title: Seasonal variation of nitrate in shallow wells of the Oued Sabra alluvial aquifer

headings.text: Seasonal variation of nitrate in shallow wells of the Oued Sabra alluvial aquifer

key_sentences: Nitrate concentrations were measured monthly in 31 hand-dug and drilled wells over two hydrological years.
Shallow wells showed a sharp rise in nitrate after the first heavy rains, while wells deeper than 20 m remained stable.
The results point to rapid leaching from latrines and livestock enclosures close to the wellheads.
Most villages along the Oued Sabra depend on shallow wells for drinking water throughout the year.
Earlier surveys sampled only once a year, at the end of the dry season, and may therefore have missed the period of greatest risk.
Samples were collected between 07:00 and 10:00, filtered on site and kept at 4 °C until analysis.
Nitrate was determined by ion chromatography within 48 hours of collection.
Six of the fourteen shallow wells exceeded 50 mg/L at least once during the wet season, compared with none of the deep wells.

tables.caption: Table 1. Mean nitrate concentration (mg/L) by season and depth class.

list_items.text: (1) Nitrate in shallow wells varies strongly with season and peaks soon after the first heavy rains.
(2) Monitoring programmes should include at least one sampling round in the early wet season.
(3) Latrines should be sited at least 30 m from wells and, where possible, downslope of them.
[1] Ibrahim, S. and Moreau, P. (2019). Groundwater quality in alluvial aquifers of the Sahel. Journal of Arid Hydrology 12, 44–61.
[2] Drylands Water Research Institute (2023). Village water point inventory, Oued Sabra basin. Internal report DW-2023-11.
[3] Tanko, A., Ndiaye, S. and Lowe, R. (2021). Sanitation distance and nitrate in shallow wells. Water and Health 9, 201–214.
